title: FTC's Operation AI Comply settles with DoNotPay over untested 'robot lawyer' claims
summary: On September 25, 2024 the FTC announced five enforcement actions under a sweep it called Operation AI Comply, including a proposed order against DoNotPay, which had marketed an AI service as the world's first robot lawyer that could generate valid legal documents and let consumers sue without a lawyer; the complaint alleged the company never tested whether the chatbot's output matched a human lawyer's work and did not hire or retain any attorneys. The proposed order requires DoNotPay to pay $193,000, notify consumers who subscribed between 2021 and 2023 about the limitations of its law-related features, and stop claiming it can substitute for any professional service without evidence to support the claim.
verification_note: URL fetched 2026-10-17; FTC press release dated September 25, 2024. DoNotPay allegations (no testing against a lawyer's work, no attorneys retained), the $193,000 payment, the 2021-2023 subscriber notices and the ban on unsupported professional-substitution claims are all confirmed from the page body. The product is a document-drafting legal service rather than a tool-using agent; kept as a governance precedent that regulators treat a missing pre-deployment Verify step as a legal defect.
